In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the digestion of DNA is inhibited by food components in a concentration-dependent manner.
protein, divalent cations, NaCl and polycation compounds inhibit the digestion of DNA, while mono-, di-, and polysaccharide do not.
the digestion of ingested DNA in vivo is affected by food components, and that the digestion efficiency depends on the composition of food and the ratio of food components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary DNA is likely to be degraded to small fragments during digestion, and then be absorbed into the blood circulation.
food components can influence the digestion of DNA in a concentration-dependent and food component-specific manner.
pepsin has a potential to digest DNA in food, but the digestion is strongly inhibited by food compositions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the digestion of DNA in the stomach is affected by food components.
the digestion of DNA in the gastrointestinal tract is affected by food composition.

food components, especially protein, carbohydrate, and cations, can inhibit the digestion of dietary DNA, which may have important implications for the fate of dietary nucleic acid in the digestive tract.
